tasks.prompt: I just took over maintenance of this repo. Who actually wrote the Python code that is still in it today, and who should I ask about records.py? Commit counts don't tell me much, I want to know whose code is really alive.
tasks.ppInvokedPrompt: Use the /project-pilot:bus-factor command for this. I just took over maintenance of this repo. Who actually wrote the Python code that is still in it today, and who should I ask about records.py? Commit counts don't tell me much, I want to know whose code is really alive.
criteria: Kenneth Reitz is named the top owner of records.py with a share of about 48% (accept 44–52%) and of all tracked Python code with about 40% (accept 36–44%); at least one of the two numbers must be given. FAIL if someone else is named top owner, if neither number is given, if a number is outside tolerance, or if the shares are derived from commit counts instead of surviving lines.

Each person who appears under several identities is listed once: Jan Vlcinsky/Vlčinský at about 12% of all Python code (accept 9–15%) and Dana Okafor/"dana okafor" at about 4.8% (accept 3–7%), if these people are listed with a number. FAIL if either appears as two separate rows or people, or if Kenneth Reitz's share is split across his two addresses.

The black-style reformat commit (Priya Raman) and the pre-commit.ci bot commit are not credited with code: Priya Raman and the bot each hold at most 1% of lines in the answer or are absent, and the answer says (in any wording) that reformatting/bot commits were looked through or left out. FAIL if Priya Raman or the bot is presented as an owner or as someone to ask, or if the answer does not mention that such commits were excluded or looked through.

Commit-heavy is not owner: Marcus Lindqvist (second-highest commit count, 25) is shown with at most 2% of live lines (truth: 0.7%, 6 lines) or not shown as an owner at all. FAIL if the answer ranks him in the top 3 owners, calls him a main owner, or recommends him as the person to ask about records.py.

The ordering after Kenneth is right for all tracked Python code: Jan Vlcinsky (about 12%) first, then Chad Whitacre and Greg Troszak (each about 8.4%, accept 6–11%), all before Dana Okafor (about 4.8%) and Tomás Ibarra (about 1.2% overall, 2% of records.py; he must be credited, not Kenneth, if mentioned). The answer states what it counted (live lines in Python files, not commits). FAIL if Dana, Marcus, Priya or the bot appear above Chad Whitacre or Greg Troszak, or if the unit counted is not stated.

tasks.prompt: We depend on this Go library and I'm worried it is a one-person project. How concentrated is the ownership of the code that is live in the repo today: what share does the top person hold, and who comes next?
tasks.ppInvokedPrompt: Use the /project-pilot:bus-factor command for this. We depend on this Go library and I'm worried it is a one-person project. How concentrated is the ownership of the code that is live in the repo today: what share does the top person hold, and who comes next?
criteria: The top owner is Fatih Arslan with about 56% of live Go lines (accept 52–60%) when tests are included, or about 58% (accept 54–62%) if the answer counts only non-test code and says so. FAIL if the share is outside tolerance, if it is computed from commits, or if someone else is the top owner.

Raj Patel and Lena Hoffmann hold at most 1% each (truth: 0.08% and 0%) or are not listed, and the answer says vendored code and generated code were left out of the count (any wording that names both vendor/ and the generated file). FAIL if either appears with more than 2%, or if the answer does not say vendored and generated files were excluded.

The `interface{}` → `any` rewrite and the move of the Attribute constants to attribute.go are not credited to Raj Patel: if the answer lists a share for Raj Patel it is at most 1%, and the answer says the mass rewrite/move was looked through (it may say so for one of the two). FAIL if Raj Patel is presented as holding more than 2% or as the owner of attribute.go.

The runners-up are correct: Linda_pp about 8.8% (accept 7–11%) and Matthew Hall about 6.7% (accept 5–8.5%), in that order, if the answer gives a number for at least one of them; for non-test-only counting Linda_pp is about 9.9% and bogem about 6.1% (accept ±2 pp). Greg Poirson (two spellings, one email) and bogem/Albert appear once each. dependabot[bot] is not named as an owner. FAIL if the order of the top three is wrong for the stated scope, if dependabot is named as an owner, or if a person is listed twice under two spellings.

A concentration conclusion with numbers: top-1 about 56% and top-3 about 71% (accept 67–75%) for the tests-included scope (non-test scope: top-1 58%, top-3 about 74%, accept 70–78%), and the conclusion that ownership is concentrated in one person. FAIL if the answer concludes ownership is evenly spread, gives a top-3 figure outside tolerance, or gives no concentration figure beyond the top-1 name.

tasks.prompt: I'm about to send a PR that touches files under src/. Who wrote the code that is actually there now, and who should I ask to review it?
tasks.ppInvokedPrompt: Use the /project-pilot:bus-factor command for this. I'm about to send a PR that touches files under src/. Who wrote the code that is actually there now, and who should I ask to review it?
criteria: Andrew Gallant is the main owner of src/ with about 77.6% of live lines (accept 74–81%) and is the main person to ask. FAIL if the share is outside 72–83%, if another person is the primary reviewer, or if the share comes from commit counts.

Sam Whitfield (license headers, module move, directory rename) holds at most 1.5% of src/ (truth: 0.2%) or is not named as an owner. If src/ancestor.rs is discussed, Andrew Gallant has about 90% of it (accept 82–95%) and Sam at most 10%. FAIL if Sam is named as a significant owner of src/, of src/ancestor.rs, or of the tests directory.

The reapplied helper is credited to its original author: Tobias Brandt holds the same_device helper in src/util.rs (about 25 lines, 56% of util.rs, accept 45–65%) and Andrew Gallant does not get those lines. FAIL if util.rs is credited mostly to Andrew Gallant, or if Tobias Brandt is absent when per-file owners are given for util.rs. (If the answer gives no per-file figures for util.rs but mentions Tobias with the helper in src/, that passes.)

The author, not the committer, is credited for the patch applied by the maintainer: Mei Tanaka is credited with the describe_file_type code in src/dent.rs (about 13 lines, 3.8% of dent.rs, accept 2–6%) and Andrew Gallant holds about 79% of dent.rs (accept 74–84%) if per-file shares are given. FAIL if Mei Tanaka is absent when dent.rs owners are listed, or if Andrew Gallant's dent.rs share is above 86%.

The answer states what it left out or merged: at least two of (license-header/boilerplate commit not counted; moved code and the renamed tests directory credited to original authors; reverted-and-reapplied change credited to its first author; author used rather than committer), and it presents everyone other than Andrew as a long tail (none above 3% of src/; Sebastian Thiel about 2.3%, Ashley about 2.3%, if named). FAIL if fewer than two such statements are present, or if any non-Andrew person is given more than 4% of src/.

tasks.prompt: Who should review a change to src/Parser/? I want whoever actually wrote the code that is there now, not whoever has the most commits.
tasks.ppInvokedPrompt: Use the /project-pilot:bus-factor command for this. Who should review a change to src/Parser/? I want whoever actually wrote the code that is there now, not whoever has the most commits.
criteria: Graham Campbell, as one person, holds about 85.5% of src/Parser/ (accept 82–89%). FAIL if his share is split into several rows or people, if the number is outside 80–91%, or if someone else is the top owner.

Priscila Duarte is credited as one person, by author rather than committer, with about 13.2% of src/Parser/ (accept 10–16.5%), and "GitHub" or "pduarte" does not appear as a separate owner. FAIL if Priscila is absent, listed below 7% or as two people, or if "GitHub" is presented as an author or owner.

Formatting commits are looked through: Marta Kowalczyk (tabs) and StyleCI Bot are each at 0% or not listed, and the answer says whitespace/format-only commits were not counted as authorship. FAIL if either appears as an owner or a suggested reviewer, or if the answer does not say such commits were excluded or looked through.

Commit count is not used as ownership: Vance Lucas (19 commits, second in commit count) is shown with at most 2% of src/Parser/ (truth: 1.0%) or not shown as owner; he is not recommended as a primary reviewer. FAIL if he is recommended first or second, or given more than 5%.

The recommendation is correct and specific: Graham Campbell first, Priscila Duarte second (for her Interpolator.php and Comments.php, where she is the author of all lines of Interpolator.php, accept ≥95%, if file-level figures are given); if the whole of src/ is mentioned, Graham holds about 92% (accept 89–95%). FAIL if the first recommendation is anyone but Graham Campbell, if Priscila is not named at all, or if a whole-src Graham figure is given outside 86–97%.

tasks.prompt: I want to change how the store proxies work (lib/rack/attack/store_proxy/). Who knows that code and should review my PR? Please only suggest people who are still around, not just the historical authors.
tasks.ppInvokedPrompt: Use the /project-pilot:bus-factor command for this. I want to change how the store proxies work (lib/rack/attack/store_proxy/). Who knows that code and should review my PR? Please only suggest people who are still around, not just the historical authors.
criteria: Hiroshi Tanaka, as one person, is credited with about 26% of lib/rack/attack/store_proxy/ (accept 22–30%) and named as someone to ask. FAIL if he is split into two people, absent, or if "GitHub" is shown as the author of his code.

Historic owners are shown as inactive and not recommended: hakanensari (about 22.7% of store_proxy, accept 19–27%, last commit 2014) and Aaron Suggs (155 commits, about 8.2% of all Ruby code, last commit 2017) are flagged as no longer active (dates or years given), and neither is recommended as a reviewer. FAIL if either is recommended, or if the answer presents the code owners without saying anything about who is no longer active.

Gonzalo Rodriguez is one person: about 18.4% of store_proxy (accept 15–22%) or about 44.6% of all Ruby code (accept 41–48%), whichever the answer reports; and he is described as still active (last commit Nov 2025). FAIL if he is split into several people, if his share is under 10% of store_proxy or under 35% of all code, or if he is called inactive.

Generated and formatting commits are not credited: Santiago Bartesaghi is at most 10.5% of all Ruby code (truth 8.4%; about 12% if the generated RBI were counted) or reported only with per-directory figures (1.8% of store_proxy), and Jonas Keller (whitespace commit) is at 0% or not listed. The answer says the generated file and the autocorrect/whitespace commits were left out or looked through. FAIL if Jonas Keller is presented as an owner, if Santiago's whole-repo share is above 11%, or if no exclusion is mentioned.

The recommendation lists only active people: it names at least one of Hiroshi Tanaka, Gonzalo Rodriguez, Santiago Bartesaghi as reviewer, with Hiroshi Tanaka or Gonzalo Rodriguez ahead of any other candidate by code ownership, and does not name anyone whose last commit is before 2024 (for example Aaron Suggs, hakanensari, fatkodima, Brad Lindsay, Jonathan del Strother) as a reviewer. FAIL if any such person is recommended, or if no active person is named.
